chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Saeed ibn Janah, from his brother Abu Aamir, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: The one who seeks the leadership, is destroyed.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of seeking leadership in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*’s chapter on seeking leadership, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies *ri'asah* (leadership/status-seeking) as a spiritual peril, warning that the desire for authority often corrupts intent and leads to ruin. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is interpreted not merely as a warning against political ambition, but as a caution against seeking position for ego or worldly gain rather than for sincere service to the community. The phrase 'seeking' implies an active, often self-centered pursuit, contrasting with the ideal of being chosen or appointed by divine will or merit.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad, from Saeed Bin Janah, from his brother Abu Aamir, from a man,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who seeks the leadership, is destroyed’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Sa’id ibn Janah from his brother, abu ‘Amir from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)
who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whoever seeks leadership is destroyed.’”
